signals.name: Any insider purchase
signals.definition: Discretionary open-market purchase (code P, non-plan, common stock) by an officer or director, >= $10,000 disclosed on one day.
signals.rationale: Baseline 'follow every insider purchase' strategy (Lakonishok & Lee 2001; Seyhun 1986).

signals.name: Cluster buying
signals.definition: >= 3 distinct officers/directors with discretionary purchases filed within 30 calendar days (triggers on the filing that completes the cluster).
signals.rationale: Independent agreement among insiders is harder to explain by liquidity or diversification needs.

signals.name: CEO / CFO purchase
signals.definition: Discretionary purchase by the company CEO or CFO (divisional titles excluded).
signals.rationale: Top executives have the broadest information set (Wang, Shin & Francis 2012 on CFOs).

signals.name: Large purchase (>= $1M)
signals.definition: Officer/director purchases totalling >= $1,000,000 disclosed on one day.
signals.rationale: Large personal capital commitment is a costly, credible signal.

signals.name: Holdings increase >= 20%
signals.definition: An insider increases directly-held shares by >= 20% in one purchase (relative to pre-trade holdings).
signals.rationale: Purchase size relative to the insider's own wealth in the stock, not absolute dollars, measures conviction.

signals.name: Buying into weakness
signals.definition: Officer/director purchase after the stock fell >= 20% over the prior 60 trading days.
signals.rationale: Contrarian insider buying: insiders may judge the decline as overdone (Jenter 2005).

signals.name: Opportunistic insider
signals.definition: Purchase by an insider who traded in each of the 3 prior years but NOT in the same calendar month (Cohen, Malloy & Pomorski 2012).
signals.rationale: Routine traders follow calendars; deviations from routine carry the information.

signals.name: First purchase in 2+ years
signals.definition: Insider's first discretionary purchase in this stock in more than 730 days (or ever, in the data).
signals.rationale: Unusual activity relative to the insider's own history.

signals.name: 10% blockholder purchase
signals.definition: Discretionary purchase >= $100,000 by a 10% owner who is not an officer or director.
signals.rationale: Activist / concentrated holders adding exposure (a bridge to the institutional analysis).

signals.name: Cluster selling (discretionary)
signals.definition: >= 3 distinct officers/directors with discretionary (non-10b5-1) sales filed within 30 days.
signals.rationale: Sales are noisier (diversification, liquidity, taxes) — tested, not assumed, to be bearish.

signals.name: CEO / CFO discretionary sale >= $1M
signals.definition: Discretionary (non-plan) sale of >= $1,000,000 by the CEO or CFO.
signals.rationale: Largest discretionary disposals by the best-informed executives.

signals.name: Rule 10b5-1 planned sales (control)
signals.definition: Officer/director sales flagged as made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan (checkbox or footnote).
signals.rationale: Pre-scheduled trades should carry little information: a built-in control group.
